pathways.title: SN2 with Cyanide
pathways.reagentNote: Draw the alkyl halide and cyanide ion as disconnected structures
pathways.shortExplanation: Cyanide attacks through carbon and displaces the leaving group in an SN2 reaction, extending the carbon skeleton by one carbon.

selectivityAssessment.label: Major pathway (qualitative)
selectivityAssessment.basis: A weakly basic nucleophile on a primary halide favors SN2 over E2. Substitution versus elimination follows the substrate class and the reagent class (Wade, Organic Chemistry, ch. 6-7 summary of SN2/E2 competition; Clayden, Greeves and Warren, ch. 17; not re-read in this stage). It is qualitative: solvent, temperature and the exact base change the ratio, and no fraction is given.

limitations: SN2 inversion is explicitly encoded at a stereogenic reacting carbon.
Secondary substrates can compete with E2.
